cds.text: Explore language used to build relationships in formal and informal situations
Understand that language is chosen for social contexts and signals social roles and relationships
Understand that language varies with levels of formality and social distance
Identify subjective language of opinion and feeling, and objective language of factual reporting
Understand how to go beyond bare assertions by considering differing ideas, opinions and authoritative sources
Understand the uses of objective and subjective language and identify bias
Listen for key points to carry out tasks and contribute to discussions, acknowledging other opinions, linking responses to the topic, and extending ideas
Use paraphrasing and questioning to clarify meaning, connect to experience, and present and justify an opinion or idea
Use paraphrasing, questioning and clarifying, with awareness of formality, to develop and support arguments and evaluate information and opinions
Plan, rehearse and deliver structured presentations to report, tell stories, recount events or argue, using subjective and objective language, complex sentences and visual features
Plan, rehearse and deliver presentations with elaborated, sequenced ideas, complex sentences, specialist vocabulary, delivery features and visual or digital features
Plan, rehearse and deliver presentations that develop a theme through arguments and details, using precise vocabulary, delivery features and visual or digital features
